ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black/dark-grey) surface area with extreme high-intensity (white) localized clusters at distal edges; macro-ratio of high-to-low intensity pixels on the ventral surface is approximately 0.05.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Continuous low-intensity dark pigmentation across >90% of the fluke surface; discrete high-intensity geometric clusters (white spots) localized at the extreme left lateral margin and extreme right distal tip.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped central indentation with an estimated pixel-based internal angle of 40-50 degrees and a vertical depth reaching approximately 15% of the visible lobe height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Irregular jagged boundary with approximately 10 primary peaks of varying amplitude (15-40 pixels) across the upper contour; highest serration frequency observed on the distal portions of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Macro-convex curvature across the superior boundary of both lobes, transitioning into a sharp vertical inflection (concave transition) at the distal right extremity.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Densely packed cluster of approximately 12-15 circular high-contrast white pixel groups on the far left lateral edge; smaller cluster of 4-6 similar high-intensity points at the far right tip.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Three distinct, near-parallel vertical linear pixel disruptions of low contrast visible in the lower-right quadrant of the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Significant structural irregularity and trailing low-intensity pixel mass at the far right distal tip, indicating either tissue amputation or attached parasitic organisms.
other_distinctive_markers: A deep, asymmetrical rectangular indentation located immediately adjacent to the left side of the median notch, distinct from the regular serration pattern.
